node_definition.done_when:
Read section 10 of the-obligations-hook-reads-a-snapshot first. On the prompt path in reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py, a reload in progress shows the last snapshot's list, headed by its age and the words producer reloading, with no remedy line. A reload is in progress when the snapshot's producer is alive and its code stamp is older than the source, or when the seat records a reload intent. No producer, and its remedy, appear only when no live producer has published for longer than a named reload-bound constant. tests/test_obligations_hook_reads_the_snapshot.py covers the reloading case, the brief-restart case and the long-absence case, each on the prompt path in a temporary configuration home, each failing at the base where it differs. Existing cases in tests/test_coordinator_obligations_hook.py keep passing; if one asserts the old not-current line for a live reloading producer, update it without deleting a case. The stop path is not part of this node.
Two constraints from a peer's measurement on 2026-10-02 (s21-fin). First, the follower already waits out a reload before warning, through producer_stale_since and _producer_reloading_event in reckon/cli.py near line 3200 (merged by stale-producer-warning-waits-for-its-reload). The hook uses that same window, through a shared function rather than a second copy, so the hook and the follower agree on when a producer is stale. Second, `reckon crew watch --ensure` answers seat-held, and changes nothing, while a live producer holds the seat. So the hook never names it as the remedy while the seat's producer is alive, and names it only when no live producer holds the seat. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
